gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-001 identifies the same false fixed-R asymptotic claim: mesh refinement leaves the upper endpoint at the finite-radius eigenvalue rather than the whole-space eigenvalue and leaves the lower-bound exterior correction. It also identifies the required joint h-to-zero and R-to-infinity limit.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries diagnose the unsupported claim that h-only refinement makes both finite-radius bounds converge exactly to the whole-space eigenvalue, despite finite-R truncation and the persistent lower-bound correction.

component_coverage.gold_component: The upper endpoint remains the finite-radius Dirichlet eigenvalue, so finite-R truncation persists under mesh refinement.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction explicitly states that the fixed-R upper bound tends to lambda_k^R greater than lambda_k and that R must also tend to infinity.

component_coverage.gold_component: The lower endpoint retains the finite-radius Neumann/exterior correction and therefore need not reach the whole-space eigenvalue under h-only refinement.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction gives the limiting lower-bound formula with the correction factor, states it can remain strictly below lambda_k, and identifies the joint R-to-infinity limit as necessary.
